headline: Exploited flaws in PAN-OS, Puppet Enterprise and LiteLLM need patching
plain_summary: Several software flaws are being used in real attacks, including in Palo Alto firewalls, Puppet Enterprise and LiteLLM. Vendors have published fixes for most of them, and a US agency has set a December 1 deadline for Puppet. Microsoft confirmed a read-only data exposure in a cloud service. Organisations running these products should check and patch.

items.title: PAN-OS management interface exploited via Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300)
items.why: Palo Alto Networks says exploitation has been observed against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.
items.action: If the management interface is reachable from the internet, upgrade immediately (for example to 12.2.4-h3, 11.2.16-h3, 11.1.16-h6 or 10.2.18-h15) and restrict access to trusted internal IPs.

items.title: CISA lists exploited Puppet Enterprise flaw CVE-2026-115731
items.why: CISA cites active exploitation; federal agencies must fix it by December 1.
items.action: Upgrade Puppet Enterprise to 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13 and restart the server; review autosign configuration as a temporary mitigation.

items.title: CISA adds Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap flaws
items.why: CISA cites active exploitation of all four, including ransomware on Synology NAS.
items.action: Find these products in your environment and apply vendor fixes where they exist; Axis 1.x is reported end of life and unpatched, so plan a migration.

items.title: Entra Connect Health API flaw exposed customer metadata
items.why: Microsoft says read-only access exposed tenant IDs, domain names and technical contacts' emails, but not passwords or keys.
items.action: Audit exposure with Microsoft's read-only PowerShell script, use phishing-resistant MFA and confirm notification recipients are legitimate.

items.title: Vortex and Cinder groups bypass MFA in Microsoft 365 attacks
items.why: Palo Alto researchers, per Borncity, describe session-token reuse and attacker-registered MFA devices followed by ransom demands.
items.action: Use phishing-resistant MFA, verify helpdesk requests, allowlist browser extensions and revoke existing sessions during incidents.

items.title: SolarWinds fixes critical Serv-U flaws, including CVE-2026-123172
items.why: The privilege escalation could give root on Linux installations; the pages read do not mention exploitation.
items.action: Update Serv-U to the fixed release named in SolarWinds' advisories.

items.title: Deichmann says attackers accessed German online-store customer data
items.why: Names, addresses, emails, phones and chosen payment method may be affected; Deichmann says passwords and payment data were not stolen.
items.action: Be alert to phishing; the company says it never asks for passwords or payment data by email, phone or SMS.

items.title: South Korea briefs industry on amended network act
items.why: Companies must designate an executive CISO, notify affected users of breaches and can face fines for repeated breaches.
